walkthroughs.body_html: 16 active missions in 2024; budget $6.4 billion. MONUSCO (DRC) is largest. Successes: Cambodia (1992-93), Sierra Leone (2005). Failures: Rwanda 1994 (800000 deaths), Srebrenica 1995. Peacekeepers from 121 countries; Bangladesh largest contributor.

UNHCR 2022: 108 million displaced globally. Syria conflict displaced 13 million (50 percent of pre-war population); 6.5 million refugees, 7 million IDPs. Turkey hosts 3.7 million; largest refugee-host country. 2015 European migration crisis: 1 million arrivals.

Russian invasion February 2022; UN General Assembly condemned 141-5. ICC arrest warrant for Putin (March 2023). EU/US sanctions; Russia removed from Council of Europe. Refugees: 8 million Ukrainians in Europe; 6 million IDPs. UN Black Sea grain deal failed July 2023.

mcqs.q: Why can a cold winter NOT disprove climate change?
options: El Nino is the name of a specific hurricane that hit Mexico.
Climate is the long-term statistical average; a single cold winter is a weather event. Climate change is the trend in averages and extremes over decades, not the absence of cold days.
Climate change only happens in summer.
A really cold winter proves global warming is not happening.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a megacity and a world city?
options: El Nino is the name of a specific hurricane that hit Mexico.
A megacity is defined by population (over 10 million); a world city is defined by global economic and cultural influence (e.g. New York, London) — so a city can be one without the other.
A megacity has over 1 million people and a world city has over 5 million.
Megacities and world cities are the same thing.

mcqs.q: What happens during an El Nino event?
options: Trade winds weaken, warm water that normally pools in the western Pacific spreads east, disrupting weather patterns globally — drought in Australia, floods in South America.
El Nino is the name of a specific hurricane that hit Mexico.
Climate change only happens in summer.
El Nino is when the ocean gets colder near Peru.
